name: kentra-agentic-plugins
description: Kentra's branded catalog of agentic coding primitives, distributed as Claude Code plugins. The primitives themselves stay neutral (own repos, MIT); this catalog is the branded distribution layer — the distribution-axis sibling of the kentra-sdlc methodology umbrella.

plugins.name: adr-sourced-constitution
plugins.description: Bootstrap skill (constitution-init) for the adr-sourced-constitution primitive: interviews and scaffolds a project's constitution (event-sourced ADR log → deterministic constitution.md). Ongoing-governance skills are installed into the governed repo by `constitution init`, not bundled here.

plugins.name: kentra-rpir
plugins.description: Runs one change through spec → plan → implement → review: interactive spec with background premise research, a milestoned-plan-dag plan an implementer follows without exploring, parallel milestones in git worktrees with a fresh verifier each, and a retro read from the session transcripts. Needs the milestoned-plan-dag CLI.

plugins.name: milestoned-plan-dag
plugins.description: Authoring skill (plan-author) for the milestoned-plan-dag primitive: the machine-first YAML plan format in which a plan is a DAG of verifiable milestones. Documents the full grammar — milestone identity, the depends-on DAG of explicit edges, the mandatory check/criteria/paths contract, plan- and milestone-level description and rules, multi-line checkbox steps — and the validate -> resolve/render CLI workflow. The CLI installs separately: `brew install kentra-io/tap/milestoned-plan-dag`.

plugins.name: kentra-skills
plugins.description: Kentra skills: java-hexagonal (framework-neutral hexagonal / ports-and-adapters layering, ArchUnit shape enforcement, and a three-tier test strategy — unit / domain-with-fakes / Testcontainers), testcontainers-java (canonical Testcontainers-Java patterns for portable integration tests — singleton containers, Kafka advertised listeners, Docker environment resolution, Ryuk under socket proxies), and subagent-workflow (an orchestrator/implementer/verifier subagent loop for executing a written implementation plan).
